claims.rule: Table2 gives measurement descriptions and a dash rather than numeric POR values for SHUNT/BUS. No numeric reset row accompanies Figure24. Exclude fixed numeric reset assertions for SV and every BUS field; software storage zero is not a hardware oracle.
At defined reset completion CONFIGURATION=0x399F, POWER=CURRENT=CALIBRATION=0; these defaults do not imply SHUNT/BUS zero.

CONFIGURATION.RST bit15 written1 generates reset equivalent to POR and self-clears. Verify restored defined defaults and RST0 only after an explicit qualified reset_completed event; pending readback and reset latency unspecified.

Figure24 labels BUS bit2 with a dash; no zero reset, write-zero, write-ignore, or dynamic value rule is given for that bit. Keep its known mask0 throughout source-common histories. Read-only register type alone cannot certify a reserved-bit value.

BUS.BD is bits15:3, unsigned4mV units; full-scale codes4000/8000 for16V/32V ranges. ADC scaling up to32V does not authorize physical input above26V. Qualified logical results have raw BD code, not measured physical voltage.

SHUNT voltage is signed two-complement with10uV units and appropriate PGA sign-extension/full-scale constraints; all-bit reset remains unknown. Qualified already encoded in-range words are supplied stimuli, not analog conversion proof.

CNVR bit1 sets only after all conversions, averaging, and multiplications complete. Partial-conversion completion is insufficient. Qualified whole_sequence_completed is an abstraction of that completion, not a timing/ADC/multiplication simulation.

Both passages support clearing CNVR when writing a changed active mode, with Power-down0 and ADC-off4 excepted. Same-mode active rewrite effect differs/ambiguous between p10 any CONFIG write and p23 new mode. Common profile clears on changed active mode, preserves under explicit0/4 exception, and invalidates CNVR after same-mode active rewrite.

Register-detail p23 says POWER read clears CNVR; p10 instead names Status read, although no Status register exists in Table2. POWER-clear is only a register_detail_candidate, not an undisputed common-source guarantee. Common profile invalidates CNVR after BUS/POWER read while preserving the pre-read value for its initial observation.

OVF bit0 is set when current or power calculations are out of range. A qualified math_overflow event may establish1; no explicit overflow clearing event, saturation/wrap, signed power, or rounding rule is supplied. No arbitrary injected overflowFalse may certify0 in common source.

Writing modes1/2/3, even when already programmed, starts a single-shot conversion. This does not specify pending sample discard policy, interleaved calibration changes, resulting MODE bits after completion, or extra convert-pin behavior.
Table5 covers all16 ADC nibble values:0X00/01/10/11 are9/10/11/12bit;8 is12bit;9..15 mean2/4/8/16/32/64/128 averages. Codes4..7 are valid aliases, not reserved. Table6 covers all8 MODE values.

CALIBRATION bit0 always0 and cannot be written1; bits15:1 store calibration. POWER/CURRENT stay0 only in the pre-first-programming default history from POR or qualified reset completion. Pages12/18 do not specify that clearing previously programmed nonzero CAL immediately resets already computed CURRENT/POWER, nor their update latency without a completed measurement/multiplication. The bounded common profile keeps these outputs unknown after later CAL clearing until a qualified reset; no immediate-zero assertion. This supporting rule does not promote calibration arithmetic or current/power physical accuracy.

Register contents update4us after write; reading same pointer at SCL>1MHz requires delay. Register-level logical operations model qualified settled transactions; no immediate silicon write/read timing proof.
